Both inputs read in full, plus the path/tier checks needed to make the manifest real. Four things I found change the plan's shape — flagged inline where they land.

---

# Cart bundle (SFCC-11) — executable build plan

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Zimmermann cart drawer and its line-item system — SFCC-315, 270, 795, 271, 272, 250, 275 — as prescribed by those seven Sprint 5 cards, as designed in Figma file `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` nodes `9323-65888/65895/65983/66104` (DEFAULT PAGE TEMPLATE) plus the CART MERGE, WISHLIST, INTERNATIONAL, EMPTY BAG and OOS state groups across all four breakpoints, as approached by the FED handbook and `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, as established in PR #85 (SFCC-236 shared product card — atoms → molecules → organism, page-level mapper, `ui-kits/<name>Shared.ts`, theme registration, `desktop/`/`mobile/` e2e split), using: the **override** approach with copy-first for `product-item/` and `item-variant/` (mirrored base files exist), the **new-component** approach under `ui-kits/` for the drawer organism, quantity stepper, inline message, actions row, button group and empty state (no mirrored base file exists), **co-located `Zimm*` recipes** for all styling, and the **existing `--zimm-*` foundation untouched** — every colour and space value in this design already exists there.

---

## 2. Scale call — six branches, and how much loop each earns

> **⚠️ SUPERSEDED by §11 (Marcel, 2026-09-17): SINGLE PR, 18 commits.**
> Retained as the record of why the seams were drawn where they were. §3's file manifest and §4's
> steps remain valid verbatim — they regroup by commit instead of by branch. §5's per-step loop
> criteria remain valid; only the per-*branch* loop scaling is replaced.

### Six branches, not one PR and not seven

| # | Branch | Stories | Files | Why it is its own branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B0** | `fix/SFCC-11_cart-e2e-area` | — (infra) | 1 | `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is **Tier 1 CI/CD**. Bundling it into a feature PR drags `@tier-1-approvers` onto a feature review and breaches AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 (one protection tier per change). |
| **B1** | `feature/SFCC-315_cart-drawer` | 315 | ~7 | **Ships first and standalone.** SFCC-316 (Jhoan, same sprint, Ready for Development) composes into it. Anything that delays this branch delays someone else's active-sprint card. |
| **B2** | `feature/SFCC-270_cart-item-override` | 270 | ~14 | **The only Tier 2 code branch.** `product-item/` pulls `@pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. Keeping it alone means one squad-B reviewer sees one coherent override, not a 40-file cart feature. Also the only branch with a mandatory copy-first pause. |
| **B3** | `feature/SFCC-795-271_cart-item-states-stepper` | 795 + 271 | ~20 | 795 and 271 are the same pixels. §5.4: "795 subsumes 270, 271 and 250's UI states — one implementation, three cards' ACs." Splitting them means building the stepper twice. |
| **B4** | `feature/SFCC-250-272_max-qty-wishlist-actions` | 250 + 272 | ~16 | **Welded, per the settled decision.** Both land in one `onAuthSuccess` callback (merge → cap → wishlist resume). They cannot be reviewed or reverted independently. |
| **B5** | `feature/SFCC-275_cart-button-group` | 275 | ~6 | Independent of the cart-item chain. Can run in parallel with B2/B3 by a second pair of hands. |

Every branch is cut fresh from an updated `develop` (`origin/develop` head `71025f18`; local is 41 behind). Never from `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch`, which carries open PR #112.

**Order:** B0 ∥ B1 first → B2 (copy-first pause) → B3 → B4. B5 any time after B0. B4 depends on B3's stepper existing and on B1's drawer hosting the empty state.

### One Tier 2 touch you cannot design away

Every branch that adds a recipe must edit `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` to register it. That file is inside `overrides/app/theme/components/` → **Tier 2**, `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. The co-location relief in CODEOWNERS (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only, last-match-wins) covers the recipe *file* and not the registration *line*. So B1, B3, B4 and B5 each carry one Tier 2 approver for a one-line import + one key. Plan for it; do not be surprised by it at PR time.

### How much loop — scaled down deliberately

| Branch | Loop | Why |
|---|---|---|
| B0 | **None.** | A workflow allow-list. Verified by observing the next cart PR's `e2e_scope` output, not by a Tester. A loop here is theatre. |
| B1 | **Light** — Tester + Scorer on one pass. | Mostly reuse: `ZimmDrawer` already owns overlay, right placement, Escape, `finalFocusRef`, mobile full-height and scroll-lock. Two things are genuinely new (the 52px reserved band, the `xLarge` width fix) and both are assertable in one `.css.test.ts`. |
| B2 | **Full loop, but only on the copy-first pass.** | The risk here is not "does it look right", it is "did the override intercept and did the 11 downstream surfaces survive". After Marcel's verification the restyle is conventional. Dropping the second loop pass. |
| B3 | **Full loop.** | Largest surface: ~25 ACs including 11 accessibility, five stepper states, three error states, two breakpoint reflows. This is where a missed state ships. |
| B4 | **Full loop, and the only step that gets a second adversarial pass.** | Async state, an auth seam, an ordered callback, a loop guard and a render guard that must not race a mutation. Highest defect cost, lowest visibility in review. |
| B5 | **Light.** | 8 ACs, six presentational, one conditional render, one stubbed destination. A two-point story does not earn a full loop. |

**Explicitly dropped, and why:** no Playwright spec on B1 (nothing to drive it — see open question 7); no `.test.ts` on the four pure-presentation atoms/molecules whose only logic is prop interpolation (`testing.md`'s single-parent exemption — covered by the organism's `play`); no separate loop pass on B2's restyle commit. Anything more would be over-scaled machinery, which is a defect in a plan.

---

## 3. File manifest

Tiers from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `protectedFiles.md`, owners read directly from `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/CODEOWNERS`. Not from `.claude/registry/*.md`.

### B0 — e2e area

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.github/workflows/qa.yml` | modify | **Tier 1 CI/CD** | `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` |

> **BLOCKED.** Named explicitly in the brief, but owner approval is not confirmed. ### B1 — SFCC-315, cart drawer organism

#### Step 1.1 — Fix `ZimmDrawer`'s `xLarge` width (this is a real bug, not a tidy-up)

**Consequence first.** `zimmDrawer.css.ts` already ships an `xLarge` size whose own comment says it is for Cart. Its value is `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'`. Figma's cart panel is a **fixed 1186px** at both 1440 and 1920 (§11.1; panel `x=256` on the 1440 frame and `x=736` on the 1920 frame — 1184 both times, so the *gap* grows and the panel does not). 82% of 1920 is **1574px** — 388px wider than designed. The inner composition is itself fixed (128 + 360 + 140 + 430 + 128 = 1186), so on a 1920 screen the shopper gets 388px of dead white space inside the panel, and the two-column layout sits off-centre. Build SFCC-315 on the existing variant unchanged and it is wrong on every large monitor.

**Mechanism.** The 82% came from a Figma frame annotation, and `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s own comment records that the *previous* reading of that same annotation was already wrong once ("that frame's annotation was wrong (or superseded)"). The annotation is a percentage; the frames are a fixed width.

**Changes.** Replace `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'` with a rem constant equal to 1186px (`74.125rem`), applied as `width`/`maxWidth` with `maxWidth: '100%'` so it cannot exceed a narrow viewport. Keep the comment convention: cite the Figma frames, state that 82% was the annotation and 1186 is the measurement, per the `zimmButton.css.ts` house pattern.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` gains an assertion that `xLarge.content` resolves to the 1186px rem value above `md`, and that `maxWidth` is `100%`.
2. No other size variant's resolved output changes — assert `large`, `tablet`, `small`, `prompt`, `mobile` snapshots are byte-identical to before.
3. `grep -rn "xLarge" overrides/app --include="*.tsx"` returns only `index.tsx`'s type union and `index.stories.tsx` — **confirmed zero production consumers today**, so blast radius is nil. Re-run this before committing; if a consumer has appeared, stop.
4. `npm run audit:tokens` does not flag the new rem constant (it carries a `// audit-allow:` or `provisional` comment naming the Figma frame, matching `PANEL_MIN_NARROW`'s existing treatment in the same file).

#### Step 4.1 — The merge call (must come first)

**Consequence first.** Today, passwordless OTP sign-in from the wishlist auth drawer does **not** merge baskets. SLAS switches the session to the registered customer and the guest basket is **orphaned — the shopper's items are gone, not miscounted.** Until this is fixed, SFCC-250's AC5 has nothing to cap and SFCC-272's AC8 has no cart item left to move. **Mechanism.** Base `use-auth-modal.js` pairs its own passwordless flow with a `mergeBasket` call. `useWishlistAuthDrawer` reimplemented passwordless login for the drawer and did not carry the merge across. The social-IDP route is fine (it redirects through base `social-login-redirect`, which merges); create-account correctly skips (a new customer has no prior basket). **Changes.** One shared function called by both the post-auth callback and the render guard — one implementation, not two copies.

**Pass criteria.**

  - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause.
  - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
  - Long leading `sleep` commands are blocked. To poll until a condition is met, use Monitor with an until-loop (e.g. `until <check>; do sleep 2; done`) — you get a notification when the loop exits. Do not chain shorter sleeps to work around the block.
 - When running `find`, search from `.` (or a specific path), not `/` — scanning the full filesystem can exhaust system resources on large trees.
 - When using `find -regex` with alternation, put the longest alternative first. Example: use `'.*\.\(tsx\|ts\)'` not `'.*\.\(ts\|tsx\)'` — the second form silently skips `.tsx` files.


# Committing changes with git

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

710	## 11.2 Cart Item (SFCC-270 / 795 / 271 / 272 / 250)
711	
712	Desktop 360x198 · mobile 338x131 · gift-card variant 226.
713	
714	| | Desktop | Mobile |
715	|---|---|---|
716	| root gap / align | 28px (space/700) / items-center | **24px (space/600) / items-start** |
717	| Image Group | 132x198, object-cover, py 12.655 | **67x100.3, object-contain, py 8.944** |
718	| Item Details gap | 12px (space/300) | **24px (space/600)** |
719	| Item Info | flex-col, name above price | **flex-row justify-between** |
720	
721	- image: aspect **288/432**, bg `alias/color/bg/surface/default` **#f6f4f1**, `mix-blend-multiply`
722	- product name: **uppercase**, `Default/Product-name` 14px / lh16 / #191919
723	- price: `Default/Price` 14px / lh18 / #191919, inner gap 8px. `PdpPrice` has a `state` prop —
724	  promotional Was/Now is a variant of it
725	- colour + size: **ONE combined string** ("Lilac Sand, One size"), `Default/Caption-strong`
726	  12px / lh18 / `text/subtle` **#666**, w 200px
727	  (SFCC-270 has separate ACs for colour and for size — two ACs, one element)
728	- quantity: gap 12px, **Icon_minus / Icon_plus 12x12px, NO touch-target wrapper**
729	- actions: gap **25px (RAW, untokenised)**, links h 24 / py 4, **capitalize**, underlined,
730	  `Default/Link-sm` 12px / lh14 / ls **-0.12px** / `link/default` #191919
731	- inline message (error/warning) sits **between the stepper and the actions**, w-full,
732	  `Default/Caption` regular 12px / lh18. In error states the Item Details gap widens 12 -> 16px.
733	- disabled steppers ship as **separate greyed SVG assets** (we use OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED = 0.4)
734	
735	Copy: fully OOS "This item is unavailable" · partial OOS "Quantity unavailable in this size"
736	
737	**Gift card variant** (out of scope, but the component API must allow it): no stepper, no actions,
738	a 5-field label/value block, annotation "Truncate message text when it goes over two lines".
739	=> build `ZimmCartItem` with the stepper and actions row **optional**. Physical gift cards render
740	as a standard 198 item; only digital is special.
741	
742	## 11.3 Cart-level-messages (SFCC-404) — NOT a simple banner
743	
744	Shell: px 128, bg white, gap 4px between stacked messages, **min-h 52 reserved even when empty**,
745	`Page-level-message` w **476px** fixed, `Message-container` gap 8px,
746	**`touchTarget` 24x24 wrapping a 20px icon**, text `Default/body2` (Futura Round regular/400,
747	14px, lh 18px).
748	
749	| Variant | Icon | Colour |
750	|---|---|---|
751	| Error | `Icon_close` | `text/error` **#9c0000** |
752	| Success | `Icon_tick` | `text/success` **#2d5a3d** |
753	| Warning | `Icon_info_solid` | `text/subtlest` **#969696** |
754	
755	**Four designer annotations define real behaviour no AC mentions:**
756	1. Empty state still reserves the space "to prevent the cart changing position depending on errors"
757	2. Errors **aggregate into one counted message** with a **live count that decrements** as the
758	   shopper resolves them; errors **always stay at the top** when stacked
759	3. Only **one success at a time**; container stays fixed, old fades out, new fades in
760	4. **Warnings are suppressed entirely** whenever an error or success is present
761	
762	=> precedence: error (pinned, aggregated) > success (single-slot, crossfade) > warning (suppressed).
763	=> full ICU pluralisation: "There **is 1** item ... **requires** action" / "There **are 2** ...
764	   **require** action".
765	=> **This is a message aggregator with severity ordering, live counting and transitions.** The
766	   "half a day" estimate given when deciding whether to pull 404 forward was wrong by a lot.
767	=> our interim Chakra toast **stacks** by default — a poorer stand-in than assumed, but still
768	   interim. Reinforces routing every message through one handler.
769	
770	Copy found: "There is 1 item in your bag that requires action" · "An item in your bag has reached
771	maximum quantity" · "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist" · "An item in your bag already exists
772	in Wishlist" · "Item added to Wishlist" (stacked — **drops the product name**)
773	
774	## 11.4 *** DISCLOSURE COPY EXISTS — corrects a decided premise ***
775	
776	The WARNINGS SHOWN state reads:
777	> **"An item in your bag has been reduced to the maximum allowed quantity"**
778	
779	Two distinct max-quantity messages exist:
780	1. "has **reached** maximum quantity" — at the cap (CART MERGE state)
781	2. "has been **reduced to** the maximum allowed quantity" — **we changed your bag**
782	
783	SFCC-250's ACs contain only #1. Disclosure was ruled out of scope **on my statement that no such
784	copy existed — that statement was wrong.** The decision stands unless Marcel revisits it, but the
785	premise was false and the copy is specced.
786	
787	## 11.5 Cart-button-group (SFCC-275)
788	
789	430x188. Button-group flex-col gap **16px** (space/400). All buttons **h 52**, px **32**
790	(space/800), min-w 80, w-full.
791	- Checkout: bg `action/primary/bg/default` **#191919**, text white, **UPPERCASE**, 14px / lh16
792	- Apple / Google Pay: 1px border `action/secondary/border/default` **#191919**; logos 48x24
793	  (absolutely positioned in Figma — a compositional shortcut; in code they are button children)
794	
795	**Verified against our atoms:** h52 == `actionSizes.height.lg`, px32 == `paddingX.lg`,
796	gap16 == `actionSizes.gap`; ZimmButton `primary` / `secondary` map exactly. No atom gap.
797	Also confirms the removed `BTN_HEIGHT_LG = 50px` provisional was wrong.
798	
799	**International:** Button-group has exactly ONE child — express buttons are **removed, not hidden**.
800	AC2's "no white gap" is a plain conditional render. Totals-summary height unchanged.
801	
802	## 11.6 Totals-summary (SFCC-274 / 816) — context for our button group
803	
804	430x857. Rows at y 0/30/60/89/118: Total Items, Shipping, Subtotal, GST, Grand Total.
805	Label 310w at x=0, value 100w at x=330 (20px gutter). **Currency symbol is its own 8px text node.**
806	3x Grand Total Container, 2 hidden => regional tax-display variants.
807	Also contains **Promotion-code** (SFCC-191, Squad B, Bianca — an accordion, border-top #e6e6e6,
808	header "ADD PROMOTION CODE", 16px chevron) and **Recommended-for-you** 430x231.
809	
810	`Recommended-for-you` swaps its heading to **"SHOP THE LOOK"** for signed-out shoppers — so a
811	**non-personalised fallback exists that does not need Einstein** (relevant: Einstein is Not
812	Deployed on all 8 sites).
813	
814	## 11.7 Empty bag (SFCC-315 AC2 / SFCC-277)
815	
816	Layout **changes**, not just copy: Cart-item-group -> 360x157; **Totals summary moves x=500 -> x=0**
817	and shrinks 430x857 -> **430x263** at y=297. Two columns collapse to one.
818	- "YOUR BAG IS EMPTY" is in the **header**, not the body
819	- the body is **Client Services contact copy**: "If you'd like some help, speak to one of our Client
820	  Services Advisors at: / +61 1800 738 895 / Monday – Saturday: 9:00AM – 5:30PM / or
821	  clientservices@zimmermann.com" (email underlined)
822	- `Default/Body 1` Futura Round Regular 16px / lh 24 / ls **-0.16px**; paragraph spacing
823	  `mb-[25px]` (RAW)
824	- **AU phone number and AU opening hours are hardcoded in the design** — must vary per storefront
825	  across 8 sites. No AC covers this.
826	
827	## 11.8 Touch targets — Figma is internally inconsistent
828	
829	| Element | Wrapper | Icon |
830	|---|---|---|
831	| Cart-level-message | named `touchTarget` **24x24** | 20 |
832	| Recommended-for-you chevrons | **24x24** | 16 |
833	| drawer/header close | **44h x 24w** | 16 |
834	| **Cart item stepper +/-** | **none** | **12** |
835	
836	"44" has provenance (close-button height) but **nothing in the design is 44x44**, which is what
837	SFCC-795's AC asks for. And the stepper has no touch target at all — 12px, half the 24px the rest
838	of the system uses. Per the house pattern (`zimmButton.css.ts`): annotate inline citing the
839	criterion and the source, add to the UI designer's open list, ship. Also **ask the designer whether
840	the stepper icons should get the same 24px touchTarget** — it reads as an oversight, not intent.
841	
842	## 11.9 Design-side issues to raise
843	
844	- stepper icons 12px with no touch target, against a 24px system convention
845	- `25px` used twice as an untokenised raw value (Item Actions gap; empty-bag paragraph spacing)
846	- two token namespaces coexist: `brand/font/*` + `alias/*` vs `default/*` + `line-height/*`
847	- two tokens resolve to the same #969696 (`text/subtlest` vs `text/muted`)
848	- stacked success drops the product name; single success keeps it
849	- SFCC-272 copy conflicts: design "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist" vs AC "[Product Name]
850	  has been moved to your wishlist"; design already-in-wishlist is a **warning** ("An item in your
851	  bag already exists in Wishlist") vs AC's **error** banner with different wording.
852	  Cards say "figma leading" => design wins, but record the divergence on 272.
853	- ~~empty-bag Client Services details are hardcoded AU~~ — **NOT an issue for this build**
854	  (Marcel, 2026-09-16): we ship a placeholder empty state only; the real one is SFCC-277's.
855	  **But the question carries to SFCC-277** — the design hardcodes `+61 1800 738 895`,
856	  "Monday – Saturday: 9:00AM – 5:30PM" and `clientservices@zimmermann.com` across 8 storefronts /
857	  6 regions. Which of those vary per region, and are hours shown in local or AU time?
858	  Flag on 277 at grooming so it isn't rediscovered mid-build.

## 11.2 Cart Item (SFCC-270 / 795 / 271 / 272 / 250)

Desktop 360x198 · mobile 338x131 · gift-card variant 226.

| | Desktop | Mobile |
|---|---|---|
| root gap / align | 28px (space/700) / items-center | **24px (space/600) / items-start** |
| Image Group | 132x198, object-cover, py 12.655 | **67x100.3, object-contain, py 8.944** |
| Item Details gap | 12px (space/300) | **24px (space/600)** |
| Item Info | flex-col, name above price | **flex-row justify-between** |

- image: aspect **288/432**, bg `alias/color/bg/surface/default` **#f6f4f1**, `mix-blend-multiply`
- product name: **uppercase**, `Default/Product-name` 14px / lh16 / #191919
- price: `Default/Price` 14px / lh18 / #191919, inner gap 8px. `PdpPrice` has a `state` prop —
  promotional Was/Now is a variant of it
- colour + size: **ONE combined string** ("Lilac Sand, One size"), `Default/Caption-strong`
  12px / lh18 / `text/subtle` **#666**, w 200px
  (SFCC-270 has separate ACs for colour and for size — two ACs, one element)
- quantity: gap 12px, **Icon_minus / Icon_plus 12x12px, NO touch-target wrapper**
- actions: gap **25px (RAW, untokenised)**, links h 24 / py 4, **capitalize**, underlined,
  `Default/Link-sm` 12px / lh14 / ls **-0.12px** / `link/default` #191919
- inline message (error/warning) sits **between the stepper and the actions**, w-full,
  `Default/Caption` regular 12px / lh18. In error states the Item Details gap widens 12 -> 16px.
- disabled steppers ship as **separate greyed SVG assets** (we use OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED = 0.4)

Copy: fully OOS "This item is unavailable" · partial OOS "Quantity unavailable in this size"

**Gift card variant** (out of scope, but the component API must allow it): no stepper, no actions,
a 5-field label/value block, annotation "Truncate message text when it goes over two lines".
=> build `ZimmCartItem` with the stepper and actions row **optional**. Physical gift cards render
as a standard 198 item; only digital is special.

## 11.3 Cart-level-messages (SFCC-404) — NOT a simple banner

Shell: px 128, bg white, gap 4px between stacked messages, **min-h 52 reserved even when empty**,
`Page-level-message` w **476px** fixed, `Message-container` gap 8px,
**`touchTarget` 24x24 wrapping a 20px icon**, text `Default/body2` (Futura Round regular/400,
14px, lh 18px).

| Variant | Icon | Colour |
|---|---|---|
| Error | `Icon_close` | `text/error` **#9c0000** |
| Success | `Icon_tick` | `text/success` **#2d5a3d** |
| Warning | `Icon_info_solid` | `text/subtlest` **#969696** |

**Four designer annotations define real behaviour no AC mentions:**
1. Empty state still reserves the space "to prevent the cart changing position depending on errors"
2. Errors **aggregate into one counted message** with a **live count that decrements** as the
   shopper resolves them; errors **always stay at the top** when stacked
3. Only **one success at a time**; container stays fixed, old fades out, new fades in
4. **Warnings are suppressed entirely** whenever an error or success is present

=> precedence: error (pinned, aggregated) > success (single-slot, crossfade) > warning (suppressed).
=> full ICU pluralisation: "There **is 1** item ... **requires** action" / "There **are 2** ...
   **require** action".
=> **This is a message aggregator with severity ordering, live counting and transitions.** The
   "half a day" estimate given when deciding whether to pull 404 forward was wrong by a lot.
=> our interim Chakra toast **stacks** by default — a poorer stand-in than assumed, but still
   interim. Reinforces routing every message through one handler.

Copy found: "There is 1 item in your bag that requires action" · "An item in your bag has reached
maximum quantity" · "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist" · "An item in your bag already exists
in Wishlist" · "Item added to Wishlist" (stacked — **drops the product name**)

## 11.4 *** DISCLOSURE COPY EXISTS — corrects a decided premise ***

The WARNINGS SHOWN state reads:
> **"An item in your bag has been reduced to the maximum allowed quantity"**

Two distinct max-quantity messages exist:
1. "has **reached** maximum quantity" — at the cap (CART MERGE state)
2. "has been **reduced to** the maximum allowed quantity" — **we changed your bag**

SFCC-250's ACs contain only #1. Disclosure was ruled out of scope **on my statement that no such
copy existed — that statement was wrong.** The decision stands unless Marcel revisits it, but the
premise was false and the copy is specced.

## 11.5 Cart-button-group (SFCC-275)

430x188. Button-group flex-col gap **16px** (space/400). All buttons **h 52**, px **32**
(space/800), min-w 80, w-full.
- Checkout: bg `action/primary/bg/default` **#191919**, text white, **UPPERCASE**, 14px / lh16
- Apple / Google Pay: 1px border `action/secondary/border/default` **#191919**; logos 48x24
  (absolutely positioned in Figma — a compositional shortcut; in code they are button children)

**Verified against our atoms:** h52 == `actionSizes.height.lg`, px32 == `paddingX.lg`,
gap16 == `actionSizes.gap`; ZimmButton `primary` / `secondary` map exactly. No atom gap.
Also confirms the removed `BTN_HEIGHT_LG = 50px` provisional was wrong.

**International:** Button-group has exactly ONE child — express buttons are **removed, not hidden**.
AC2's "no white gap" is a plain conditional render. Totals-summary height unchanged.

## 11.6 Totals-summary (SFCC-274 / 816) — context for our button group

430x857. Rows at y 0/30/60/89/118: Total Items, Shipping, Subtotal, GST, Grand Total.
Label 310w at x=0, value 100w at x=330 (20px gutter). **Currency symbol is its own 8px text node.**
3x Grand Total Container, 2 hidden => regional tax-display variants.
Also contains **Promotion-code** (SFCC-191, Squad B, Bianca — an accordion, border-top #e6e6e6,
header "ADD PROMOTION CODE", 16px chevron) and **Recommended-for-you** 430x231.

`Recommended-for-you` swaps its heading to **"SHOP THE LOOK"** for signed-out shoppers — so a
**non-personalised fallback exists that does not need Einstein** (relevant: Einstein is Not
Deployed on all 8 sites).

## 11.7 Empty bag (SFCC-315 AC2 / SFCC-277)

Layout **changes**, not just copy: Cart-item-group -> 360x157; **Totals summary moves x=500 -> x=0**
and shrinks 430x857 -> **430x263** at y=297. Two columns collapse to one.
- "YOUR BAG IS EMPTY" is in the **header**, not the body
- the body is **Client Services contact copy**: "If you'd like some help, speak to one of our Client
  Services Advisors at: / +61 1800 738 895 / Monday – Saturday: 9:00AM – 5:30PM / or
  clientservices@zimmermann.com" (email underlined)
- `Default/Body 1` Futura Round Regular 16px / lh 24 / ls **-0.16px**; paragraph spacing
  `mb-[25px]` (RAW)
- **AU phone number and AU opening hours are hardcoded in the design** — must vary per storefront
  across 8 sites. No AC covers this.

## 11.8 Touch targets — Figma is internally inconsistent

| Element | Wrapper | Icon |
|---|---|---|
| Cart-level-message | named `touchTarget` **24x24** | 20 |
| Recommended-for-you chevrons | **24x24** | 16 |
| drawer/header close | **44h x 24w** | 16 |
| **Cart item stepper +/-** | **none** | **12** |

"44" has provenance (close-button height) but **nothing in the design is 44x44**, which is what
SFCC-795's AC asks for. And the stepper has no touch target at all — 12px, half the 24px the rest
of the system uses. Per the house pattern (`zimmButton.css.ts`): annotate inline citing the
criterion and the source, add to the UI designer's open list, ship. Also **ask the designer whether
the stepper icons should get the same 24px touchTarget** — it reads as an oversight, not intent.

## 11.9 Design-side issues to raise

- stepper icons 12px with no touch target, against a 24px system convention
- `25px` used twice as an untokenised raw value (Item Actions gap; empty-bag paragraph spacing)
- two token namespaces coexist: `brand/font/*` + `alias/*` vs `default/*` + `line-height/*`
- two tokens resolve to the same #969696 (`text/subtlest` vs `text/muted`)
- stacked success drops the product name; single success keeps it
- SFCC-272 copy conflicts: design "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist" vs AC "[Product Name]
  has been moved to your wishlist"; design already-in-wishlist is a **warning** ("An item in your
  bag already exists in Wishlist") vs AC's **error** banner with different wording.
  Cards say "figma leading" => design wins, but record the divergence on 272.
- ~~empty-bag Client Services details are hardcoded AU~~ — **NOT an issue for this build**
  (Marcel, 2026-09-16): we ship a placeholder empty state only; the real one is SFCC-277's.
  **But the question carries to SFCC-277** — the design hardcodes `+61 1800 738 895`,
  "Monday – Saturday: 9:00AM – 5:30PM" and `clientservices@zimmermann.com` across 8 storefronts /
  6 regions. Which of those vary per region, and are hours shown in local or AU time?
  Flag on 277 at grooming so it isn't rediscovered mid-build.

871	textStyle, not var-by-var:
872	`Default/body2`→`body2` · `body2-strong`→`body2Strong` · `Caption`→`caption` ·

881	**`--zimm-color-text-muted`**. No ambiguity in our system.
882	**Bonus — every colour in the cart design already exists in our foundation. No new tokens needed:**
883	| Figma | Ours |
884	|---|---|
885	| `text/default` #191919 | `grey[900]` → `--zimm-color-text-default` |
886	| `text/subtle` #666 | `grey[600]` → `text.secondary` |
887	| `text/subtlest` + `text/muted` #969696 | `grey[300]` → `text.muted` |
888	| `text/error` #9c0000 | `red[500]` → **`status.error`** |
889	| `text/success` #2d5a3d | `green[500]` → **`status.success`** |
890	| `bg/surface/default` #f6f4f1 | `ivory[200]` |
891	| `border/default` #e6e6e6 | `grey[100]` → `border.default` |
892	
893	**(7) Warning typography — DRIFT, conclusively.** Checked desktop + mobile. The WARNINGS SHOWN
894	state is off-pattern in **four** ways at both breakpoints:
895	- `Default/Body 2 Medium` (Medium/500, ls −0.14px) vs every other message's `Default/body2`
896	  (regular/400, ls 0)
897	- **`px-[128px]` hardcoded** instead of `var(--alias/space/3200)` — and it is on a **mobile** frame
898	  where the gutter should be 32px
899	- **`text-[#969696]` hardcoded hex** instead of the token var
900	- `Page-level-message` `w-full` instead of the established `w-[476px]`
901	Its mobile header is also 68px where the default mobile frame's is 108px.
902	=> built separately, off-pattern. **Implement WARNINGS SHOWN using the established message pattern**
903	   (body2, `--zimm-color-text-muted`, tokenised gutter), not its own styling.
904	
905	**(8) Stacked success drops the product name — INTENTIONAL by prevalence.** Generic
906	("Item added to Wishlist") at **both** desktop and mobile in the stacked state; product-named
907	("Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist") in the single state. Consistent in both states, so per
908	the one-off-vs-prevalent test it is deliberate compaction.
909	**But worth confirming rather than silently following:** it drops the single most useful piece of
910	information exactly when there is more on screen, and it conflicts with SFCC-272's AC, which
911	specifies `[Product Name]` in all cases.
912	
913	**(9) Odd computed numbers — ROOT FOUND. Two separate causes.**
914	- **The decimal paddings are post-scale rendered values of real tokens.** Proof: `alias/space/1200`
915	  reports fallback **48px** on the empty-bag cart-item-group gap and **12.655px** on the cart item
916	  image; `alias/space/1000` reports **40px** on the header/recommendations and **8.944px** on the
917	  mobile cart item image. Same token, different fallback => the decimal is what Figma rendered after
918	  scaling, not the token value. **Use the token (48 / 40), never the decimal.**
919	- **Tablet 659.2 is a computed fill width, not a spec.** `659.2 = 595.2 content + 2 × 32 gutter`;
920	  the gutter is a real token (32px). Confirmed NOT a uniformly scaled instance — the tablet header
921	  is its own 92px and the message band is exactly 52 (unscaled).
922	  **Implement tablet as a fluid width with a 32px gutter, never a hardcoded 659.2.**

925	| | Panel | Layout | Gutter | Header |
926	|---|---|---|---|---|
927	| Desktop 1440+ | **fixed 1186px** | two-column (items 360 / totals 430, 140 gutter) | 128 | 84 |
928	| Tablet 834 | fluid (~79%) | **single column** | **32** | 92 |
929	| Mobile 402 | full-width | single column | 32 | 108 (68 in some states — drift) |

932	- **The mobile message band hardcodes `px-[128px]` across multiple states** — should be 32px.
933	  Systematic, not a one-off.
934	- **Mobile header height varies by state**: 108 (default) vs 68 (error states).
935	- **Within a single node, one message is `w-full` and the next is `w-[476px]`** (mobile
936	  warnings-hidden). Clear drift.
937	
938	## 11.11 Final three design items — SETTLED (Marcel, 2026-09-16). None go to the designer as questions.
939	
940	**(1) Stepper touch target — BUILD 24px.** Wrap each 12x12 glyph in an invisible 24x24 centred box.
941	Justified three ways independently: our own atoms already use 24 (`zimmButton`, `zimmTextInput`,
942	`zimmNavItem`, `footerNavColumn` — all `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`), the design's own node is literally
943	named `touchTarget` at 24, and WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 sets 24 as the minimum (AGENTS.md targets 2.2 AA).
944	Use `ZimmButton`'s `icon` size — it is already `minW`/`minH: var(--zimm-scale-xl)`, and its comment
945	explains why it must be minW/minH rather than padding (Chakra `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: 0`
946	as a style prop that merges after `__css`, so recipe padding is silently dropped).
947	**Gap: use 8px (`xs`)** -> 14px apparent, since a 24 box adds 6px invisible padding each side and
948	there is no 6px token (scale jumps 4 -> 8 -> 12). 4 and 8 are equidistant from the design's 12;
949	8 is chosen because erring toward more space is correct for a touch control.
950	Annotate: design showed a 12px glyph with no touch target and a 12px gap; we applied the system's 24.
951	
952	**(2) Stacked success message — FOLLOW THE DESIGN: drop the product name when other messages are
953	present.** Single message -> "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist". Stacked -> "Item added to
954	Wishlist". (Marcel overrode the recommendation to keep the name in both cases.)
955	**Two consequences to build for:**
956	- The copy is **two strings selected by stack state**, not one string with a placeholder. The
957	  message emitter must know whether other messages are present to choose. That couples copy
958	  selection to the aggregator's state — a real requirement for SFCC-404.
959	- **The interim Chakra toast uses the product-named copy.** A toast has no aggregation concept and
960	  is always "on its own" from the shopper's point of view; the generic variant only becomes
961	  reachable once 404 lands with real stacking.
962	- Diverges from SFCC-272's AC, which specifies `[Product Name]` in all cases. Cards are "figma
963	  leading" and are not edited -> record on the 272 comment.
964	
965	**(3) Mobile drift — use our own values, not the drifted nodes.**
966	- gutter on mobile -> **32px** (the 128px in those nodes is the desktop value left on a mobile frame)
967	- message width on mobile -> **full width** (476px is the desktop value; it is wider than the 402
968	  viewport)
969	- header height -> **whatever `ZimmDrawer` already implements**. Its header sizing was reconciled
970	  against Figma during SFCC-831/926, so it has already been through the designer. Do NOT re-derive
971	  from these nodes, which disagree with each other (108 vs 68).
972	
973	**Nothing in §11.9–11.11 blocks the build, and NO message goes to the UI designer** — Marcel,
974	2026-09-16: these sit within the developer's own decisions. The divergences are handled by
975	annotating inline at the point of use, per the house pattern in `zimmButton.css.ts` (cite the
976	criterion, name the source, say what was applied and why). §11.9's list stays as a record of what
977	was found, not as an open action on anyone.

named `touchTarget` at 24, and WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 sets 24 as the minimum (AGENTS.md targets 2.2 AA).
Use `ZimmButton`'s `icon` size — it is already `minW`/`minH: var(--zimm-scale-xl)`, and its comment
explains why it must be minW/minH rather than padding (Chakra `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: 0`
as a style prop that merges after `__css`, so recipe padding is silently dropped).
**Gap: use 8px (`xs`)** -> 14px apparent, since a 24 box adds 6px invisible padding each side and
there is no 6px token (scale jumps 4 -> 8 -> 12). 4 and 8 are equidistant from the design's 12;
8 is chosen because erring toward more space is correct for a touch control.
Annotate: design showed a 12px glyph with no touch target and a 12px gap; we applied the system's 24.

**(2) Stacked success message — FOLLOW THE DESIGN: drop the product name when other messages are
present.** Single message -> "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist". Stacked -> "Item added to
Wishlist". (Marcel overrode the recommendation to keep the name in both cases.)
**Two consequences to build for:**
- The copy is **two strings selected by stack state**, not one string with a placeholder. The
  message emitter must know whether other messages are present to choose. That couples copy
  selection to the aggregator's state — a real requirement for SFCC-404.
- **The interim Chakra toast uses the product-named copy.** A toast has no aggregation concept and
  is always "on its own" from the shopper's point of view; the generic variant only becomes
  reachable once 404 lands with real stacking.
- Diverges from SFCC-272's AC, which specifies `[Product Name]` in all cases. Cards are "figma
  leading" and are not edited -> record on the 272 comment.

**(3) Mobile drift — use our own values, not the drifted nodes.**
- gutter on mobile -> **32px** (the 128px in those nodes is the desktop value left on a mobile frame)
- message width on mobile -> **full width** (476px is the desktop value; it is wider than the 402
  viewport)
- header height -> **whatever `ZimmDrawer` already implements**. Its header sizing was reconciled
  against Figma during SFCC-831/926, so it has already been through the designer. Do NOT re-derive
  from these nodes, which disagree with each other (108 vs 68).

**Nothing in §11.9–11.11 blocks the build, and NO message goes to the UI designer** — Marcel,
2026-09-16: these sit within the developer's own decisions. The divergences are handled by
annotating inline at the point of use, per the house pattern in `zimmButton.css.ts` (cite the
criterion, name the source, say what was applied and why). §11.9's list stays as a record of what
was found, not as an open action on anyone.

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { ZimmIcon } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon';
4	
5	const ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE = 'ZimmInlineMessage';
6	
7	export type ZimmInlineMessageProps = {
8	  /**
9	   * Colour/severity only — this atom never decides which one applies. A caller may legitimately
10	   * pass `variant="warning"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word "error" (the cart
11	   * max-quantity message is exactly this case) — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for
12	   * why that's a deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation, not a mismatch to fix here.
13	   */
14	  variant: 'error' | 'warning';
15	  /**
16	   * Message copy, rendered verbatim. This atom never derives, hardcodes, or paraphrases copy — a
17	   * caller supplies the already-resolved string (e.g. "This item is unavailable", "Quantity
18	   * unavailable in this size", "Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size" — SFCC-795
19	   * §11.2 exact copy).
20	   */
21	  text: string;
22	};
23	
24	/**
25	 * Atom — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2). Presentation only:
26	 * renders whatever `variant`/`text` it is given and never determines availability itself.
27	 * OOS/partial-OOS detection is SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's — both
28	 * later-sprint tickets this component does not, and should not, anticipate. No low-stock variant
29	 * exists in `ZimmInlineMessageProps['variant']` — a separate requirement explicitly forbids
30	 * low-stock messaging at the cart level (see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts).
31	 *
32	 * `aria-live="polite"` matches the same treatment this codebase already gives another transient,
33	 * non-input cart-line status value — ZimmQuantityStepper's own quantity display (its `value`
34	 * part, zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx) carries the identical `aria-live="polite"` treatment — so
35	 * a shopper using assistive tech is told about a message that appears/changes after their own
36	 * action, without requiring focus to move to it.
37	 *
38	 * SFCC-795 rework (Marcel's own visual checkpoint against the real Figma file): the `warning`
39	 * variant renders a leading `info-solid` icon, `error` never does — confirmed against 3 real
40	 * cart-item instances in Figma file QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs: the two error-copy states (FULLY OOS
41	 * node 9323-101979, PARTIAL OOS node 9323-98397) have no icon in their message sub-tree; the
42	 * warning-copy state (WARNINGS SHOWN node 9323-106685) does. The icon is `aria-hidden` — the
43	 * message's own text plus `aria-live` already carry the full meaning to assistive tech, so the
44	 * icon is a purely visual (sighted-only) reinforcement of a severity already conveyed by colour
45	 * and copy, not an independent piece of information.
46	 *
47	 * @param props see ZimmInlineMessageProps
48	 */
49	export const ZimmInlineMessage = ({ variant, text }: ZimmInlineMessageProps) => {
50	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE, { variant });
51	
52	  return (
53	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} aria-live="polite" data-testid="zimm-inline-message">
54	      {variant === 'warning' && <ZimmIcon type="info-solid" size="md" aria-hidden />}
55	      <chakra.p __css={styles.text}>{text}</chakra.p>
56	    </chakra.div>
57	  );
58	};
59

1	/**
2	 * Recipe — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2).
3	 * `.claude/session-notes.md` §11.2: "inline message (error/warning) sits between the stepper and
4	 * the actions, w-full, `Default/Caption` regular 12px / lh18. In error states the Item Details
5	 * gap widens 12 -> 16px." (the gap widening is `ZimmCartItem`'s own `hasError` resolution prop —
6	 * see product-item.css.ts — not this recipe's concern; this file owns only the message's own
7	 * type/colour/icon.)
8	 *
9	 * Two-part multipart recipe (`root`/`text`), following zimmDrawer.css.ts's plain-object
10	 * `{parts, baseStyle, variants}` shape rather than `defineStyleConfig` — no Chakra helper
11	 * factory, same Chakra-native string `variants` resolution either form supports.
12	 *
13	 * Restructured from a single-node `defineStyleConfig` (SFCC-795 rework — Marcel's own visual
14	 * checkpoint against the real Figma file surfaced a genuine gap the original single-node shape
15	 * couldn't express): the `warning` variant carries a leading 16x16 icon, the `error` variant
16	 * never does. Confirmed against 3 real cart-item instances in Figma file
17	 * QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs ("Zimmermann_Designs") — the two error-copy states (FULLY OOS node
18	 * 9323-101979, PARTIAL OOS node 9323-98397) have a bare `<text>` message sub-tree, no icon; the
19	 * warning-copy state (WARNINGS SHOWN node 9323-106685) is `icon(16x16, x=0) -> 8px gap ->
20	 * text(x=24)`. So the single implicit node this recipe used to describe is no longer enough:
21	 * `root` is now the flex row wrapping the optional icon + the text, and `text` carries what used
22	 * to be the whole recipe's `baseStyle`.
23	 *
24	 * No separate `icon` part: `ZimmIcon`'s own `color` prop defaults to `currentColor`
25	 * (zimmIcon/index.tsx), and Chakra's `Icon` component passes `color` straight through as the
26	 * rendered SVG's own inline CSS `color` rather than resolving it to a token itself (confirmed
27	 * directly in `@chakra-ui/icon`'s `Icon` implementation) — so the icon element's own
28	 * `stroke="currentColor"` shapes (zimm.tsx's `InfoSolidIcon`) inherit `root`'s `color` via
29	 * ordinary CSS inheritance for free. Nothing to declare on this recipe's side for the icon.
30	 *
31	 * --- Typography: regular weight is a DELIBERATE override, on a DIFFERENT Figma node than the
32	 * one commit 5 (SFCC-270) corrected — read both before touching either ---
33	 * `textStyle: 'caption'` supplies the correct 12px size / 18px line-height pair, but this
34	 * codebase's `caption` textStyle (theme/foundation/typography.ts) is MEDIUM-weight
35	 * (`fontWeight: fontWeights.medium`) — that is exactly right for Figma's OTHER caption node,
36	 * `Default/Caption-strong` (the cart-item colour+size line — see
37	 * item-variant/item-variant.css.ts:73-84, which deliberately keeps `caption` with NO fontWeight
38	 * override for that reason, having removed an earlier, backwards override). THIS element is
39	 * Figma's plain, un-strong `Default/Caption` node, which is REGULAR-weight per the session-notes
40	 * citation above — the opposite correction, on a different string, elsewhere in the same design
41	 * file. `fontWeight` is therefore set explicitly below, on the `text` part, to override the
42	 * textStyle-expanded medium value back down to regular — the same "a direct CSS prop applied
43	 * after the textStyle expansion wins in Chakra's style pipeline" mechanism zimmButton.css.ts's
44	 * `sizes.lg`/`sizes.sm` already documents and relies on for the identical reason.
45	 *
46	 * `root.width: 'full'` reproduces Figma's own "w-full" annotation for this element explicitly,
47	 * rather than relying on this node's flex/stack parent to stretch it by default — moved here
48	 * from the (no-longer-existing) single node, since `root` is now the outer container.
49	 *
50	 * `root.alignItems: 'flex-start'`: top-aligned, not centred — the warning icon sits at the top
51	 * of what can be 2-line-wrapped text, not vertically centred against it. Confirmed via the
52	 * Figma metadata's own y-positions on the WARNINGS SHOWN node: the icon instance sits at y=0
53	 * within its frame, the same top edge the text frame starts from.
54	 *
55	 * `root.gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'` (8px): the WARNINGS SHOWN node places the 16px-wide icon at
56	 * x=0 and the text frame starting at x=24 — the 8px difference between them is the gap.
57	 *
58	 * No low-stock variant: a separate requirement explicitly forbids low-stock messaging at the
59	 * cart level (SFCC-795 §11.2 build decisions) — the variants map below only ever has the two
60	 * keys `error`/`warning`; do not add a third.
61	 */
62	const baseStyle = {
63	  root: {
64	    display: 'flex',
65	    alignItems: 'flex-start',
66	    gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
67	    width: 'full',
68	  },
69	  text: {
70	    textStyle: 'caption',
71	    fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-regular)',
72	    // Standard flexbox text-truncation-prevention: without these, a long message next to the
73	    // fixed-size icon in this flex row can be squeezed narrower than its own content instead of
74	    // wrapping onto its own available width. `flex: 1` lets the text claim the row's remaining
75	    // space (the icon, an intrinsically-sized SVG, takes only what it needs); `minWidth: 0`
76	    // overrides a flex item's own default `min-width: auto`, which would otherwise refuse to
77	    // shrink the text below its content's intrinsic width and push `root` wider than its own
78	    // `width: full`.
79	    flex: 1,
80	    minWidth: 0,
81	  },
82	};
83	
84	const variants = {
85	  // Figma `text/error` #9c0000 -> status.error (session-notes.md §11.10(6) colour audit).
86	  error: {
87	    root: {
88	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-status-error)',
89	    },
90	  },
91	  // Figma `text/muted` / `text/subtlest` #969696 -> both collapse onto this one token, no
92	  // ambiguity in this codebase's own set (session-notes.md §11.10(6)). This is also the same
93	  // token the InfoSolidIcon's own real Figma export colour (#969696) coincidentally matches —
94	  // see that icon's own citation in zimm.tsx — not a second, independent confirmation of the
95	  // token choice, just a coincidence worth noting there and here.
96	  //
97	  // Max-quantity messaging ("Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size") uses THIS variant,
98	  // not `error` — even though its own requirement/AC text uses the word "error" to describe it.
99	  // That word is describing "user-facing feedback" in the requirement's own vocabulary, not
100	  // asserting the error SEVERITY tier: the actual Figma design and that story's own AC agree the
101	  // rendered treatment is grey/warning, not red/error. Deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation,
102	  // settled at this build's planning gate — not a mistake, and not to be "corrected" back to
103	  // `error` by a future reader matching the word alone.
104	  warning: {
105	    root: {
106	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-muted)',
107	    },
108	  },
109	};
110	
111	export const ZimmInlineMessage = {
112	  parts: ['root', 'text'],
113	  baseStyle,
114	  variants,
115	};

411	  use the bridge pattern (faithful default export, styling in a recipe).

Verdict: **IN SCOPE**, with two named follow-ups Marcel should still close before this merges (neither blocks the commit itself, both are cheap). No Tier 1 file touched. 16 files total, all traceable either to the plan step 3.2 manifest or to the now-corroborated icon fix — but "corroborated" took real digging, and I want to show that work rather than just co-sign it, because my first pass through the docs pointed the other way.

## The scope question you asked me to independently judge

My first read said this was scope creep pulled in from the wrong ticket. Here's why, and then why I reversed it — both matter, because the reversal only holds up if you check the same thing I did.

**What made me suspicious.** `.claude/session-notes.md` §11.2 (line 731) — the detailed, pixel-level Figma breakdown for exactly this ticket group (SFCC-270/795/271/272/250) — describes the inline message with no icon at all: *"inline message (error/warning) sits between the stepper and the actions, w-full, `Default/Caption` regular 12px / lh18."* The plan's own step 3.2 text matches that silence — "New atom, variant-driven: `error` / `warning`" — no icon, and none of its 6 pass criteria mention one. The *only* other place `Icon_info_solid` appears anywhere in session-notes.md is §11.3 (line 753), which is explicitly a **different ticket** (SFCC-404, cart-level message band) that the brief itself says is "correctly not conflated" — except the brief's own description of that ticket has it backwards (it says SFCC-404's icon is on the Error variant; line 751/753 say Error uses `Icon_close`, and it's the *Warning* row that carries `Icon_info_solid` — the exact variant the rework just added it to). §11.10 finding (7) also already discusses a state literally named "WARNINGS SHOWN" — but every attribute it lists (`Page-level-message` 476px, `px-[128px]` shell, a mobile header that varies 108 vs 68) is page/band-level, not per-item. That's not proof, but it's a real, specific reason to doubt the node citation in the new code (`overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx:493-501`, `zimmInlineMessage/index.tsx:38-45`, `zimmInlineMessage.css.ts:13-22` — all three cite "WARNINGS SHOWN node 9323-106685" as their source).

**Why I reversed.** Session-notes.md line 395 — the *original* SFCC-795 ticket restatement, written before any of the later Figma-metadata deep dives — already says, independently of all the above: *"warning state (grey info icon + message, e.g. 'Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size')."* That's the exact copy string the rework uses, and it predates the live Figma checkpoint entirely. The plan itself (`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-11/plan.md` §10, lines 712-767) also shows the planner was fully aware icons needed sourcing-and-verification work in this same bundle — it has a whole worked example for the stepper's `+` icon and a separate one for the Apple/Google Pay marks, both citing the identical AGENTS.md rule ("if a required icon is missing, ask — don't substitute") the rework followed here. There's no equivalent entry for the inline-message icon anywhere in the plan. Put together: the icon was a real, already-known SFCC-795 requirement that got dropped somewhere between the ticket restatement and the written step 3.2 — not something invented or borrowed from SFCC-404. Marcel's checkpoint caught a genuine under-delivery in the plan/build, not a design element that doesn't belong. That's why my verdict is IN SCOPE, not OVER.

**What I couldn't close, and why it's a follow-up, not a blocker.** I have no Figma access in this session (no MCP tool was in my kit), so I can't independently open node `9323-106685` and check whether it's a per-item component instance or the SFCC-404 page-level frame §11.10(7) was describing. The *qualitative* requirement (grey icon exists on the warning variant) is solid on the line-395 evidence above. The *exact pixel values* now shipped off that node citation (16×16, no touch-target wrapper, 8px gap, #969696) are plausible but not independently re-confirmed by me — and they happen to line up closely with SFCC-404's spec (line 753, Message-container gap 8px).
